testName: IISER IAT - Organic Compounds Containing Nitrogen: Amines, Diazonium Salts (20 Questions)
subject: Chemistry

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a secondary amine?
questions.explanation: Classification based on number of alkyl/aryl groups attached to nitrogen: Primary (1°): RNH2 (one group) - CH3NH2, C6H5NH2; Secondary (2°): R2NH (two groups) - (CH3)2NH; Tertiary (3°): R3N (three groups) - (CH3)3N. (CH3)2NH (dimethylamine) has two methyl groups attached to nitrogen, making it a secondary amine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The correct order of basicity in aqueous solution is:
questions.explanation: Basicity depends on availability of lone pair on nitrogen for protonation. In aqueous solution, two factors operate: Inductive effect (+I) increases basicity (more alkyl groups = more basic); Solvation (H-bonding) decreases basicity (more H atoms = better solvation = more stable cation). For secondary amines, both factors are balanced optimally. Order: (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N > NH3. In gas phase, order is (CH3)3N > (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > NH3 (only inductive effect matters).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used to prepare:
questions.explanation: Gabriel synthesis uses phthalimide + KOH → potassium phthalimide. Potassium phthalimide reacts with alkyl halide (SN2) → N-alkylphthalimide. Hydrolysis or hydrazinolysis yields primary amine (R-NH2). This method gives pure primary amines without secondary/tertiary contamination. Aromatic amines (aniline) CANNOT be prepared because aryl halides don't undergo SN2. Secondary and tertiary amines cannot be prepared because phthalimide has only one acidic hydrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction converts:
options: Amide to amine with same number of carbons
Amide to amine with one less carbon
questions.explanation: Hofmann degradation: R-CONH2 + Br2 + 4NaOH → R-NH2 + Na2CO3 + 2NaBr + 2H2O. This converts a primary amide to a primary amine. The carbon chain loses one carbon (as CO3^2-). Mechanism involves isocyanate intermediate formation via rearrangement. Example: CH3CONH2 (acetamide, 2C) → CH3NH2 (methylamine, 1C). Key point: Chain length decreases by one carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Benzene diazonium chloride on treatment with phenol in alkaline medium gives:
questions.explanation: This is an azo coupling reaction (diazo coupling). Benzene diazonium chloride (electrophile) couples with phenol (activated aromatic ring). The coupling occurs at para position of phenol (ortho is sterically hindered). Product is p-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange azo dye. This is an important reaction for synthesis of azo dyes. Chlorobenzene from Sandmeyer; Benzene from hypophosphorous acid; Aniline is starting material for diazonium salt.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of benzene diazonium chloride with CuCl gives:
questions.explanation: Sandmeyer reaction replaces diazonium group with halogen or cyano group. Reagents: CuX (X = Cl, Br) or CuCN for cyanide replacement. C6H5N2+Cl- + CuCl → C6H5Cl + N2 + CuCl2. Product is chlorobenzene. This is the best method to introduce halogen on benzene ring (better than direct halogenation). Gattermann reaction uses Cu/HCl instead of CuCl.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The carbylamine reaction is used as a test for:
questions.explanation: Carbylamine reaction: R-NH2 + CHCl3 + 3KOH → R-NC + 3KCl + 3H2O. Primary amine reacts with chloroform and KOH to form isocyanide (carbylamine). Isocyanides have characteristic offensive odor (like rotten fish). This test is specific for PRIMARY amines only. Secondary and tertiary amines do not give this test. This is also called isocyanide test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Hinsberg test uses:
questions.explanation: Hinsberg test distinguishes 1°, 2°, and 3° amines. Reagent: Benzenesulfonyl chloride (C6H5SO2Cl) or tosyl chloride. Observations: 1° amine forms sulfonamide soluble in NaOH (acidic H present); 2° amine forms sulfonamide insoluble in NaOH (no acidic H); 3° amine has no reaction (does not form sulfonamide). This is based on the presence or absence of replaceable hydrogen on nitrogen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid (NaNO2/HCl) at 0-5°C to give:
questions.explanation: Primary aliphatic amine + HNO2 → Unstable aliphatic diazonium salt. Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and immediately decompose. R-NH2 + HNO2 → R-OH + N2↑ + H2O (nitrogen gas evolved). This is different from aromatic amines which form stable diazonium salts. The evolution of N2 gas is a test for primary aliphatic amines. Secondary amines give N-nitroso compounds (yellow oil); Tertiary amines do not react.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The reduction of nitrobenzene in neutral medium (Zn/NH4Cl) gives:
questions.explanation: Different reduction conditions give different products from nitrobenzene: Acidic (Sn/HCl) gives Aniline (complete reduction); Neutral (Zn/NH4Cl) gives N-phenylhydroxylamine (partial reduction); Alkaline (Zn/NaOH) gives various products (azoxybenzene, hydrazobenzene, etc.). Zn dust + NH4Cl (neutral) reduces nitrobenzene to N-phenylhydroxylamine (C6H5NHOH). This is an important intermediate in the Bamberger rearrangement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aniline undergoes bromination with Br2/H2O to give:
questions.explanation: The -NH2 group strongly activates the benzene ring toward electrophilic substitution. +R effect of nitrogen donates electron density to ortho and para positions. Aniline is highly reactive (more than phenol). With Br2/H2O (aqueous bromine), all three positions (2, 4, 6) are substituted. Product is 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (white precipitate). Monobromination requires non-polar solvent (CCl4) and limited bromine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Acylation of amines with acetyl chloride is carried out in presence of base to:
options: Remove the HCl formed and prevent salt formation
questions.explanation: Acylation: R-NH2 + CH3COCl → R-NHCOCH3 + HCl. HCl is produced as byproduct. HCl reacts with unreacted amine to form salt: R-NH2 + HCl → R-NH3+Cl-. This removes free amine from reaction, decreasing yield. Base (pyridine or NaOH) neutralizes HCl: Base + HCl → Salt + H2O. This prevents salt formation and maintains free amine concentration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hofmann elimination of quaternary ammonium hydroxides gives:
options: A mixture of both alkenes equally
questions.explanation: Hofmann elimination: R4N+OH- (heated) → Alkene + R3N + H2O. This is E2 elimination from quaternary ammonium hydroxides. Unlike Zaitsev's rule, Hofmann elimination gives the LESS substituted alkene. Reason: The leaving group (NR3) is bulky, so base attacks the less hindered β-hydrogen. Example: CH3CH2CH(CH3)N+(CH3)3OH- → CH3CH=CHCH3 (minor) + CH3CH2CH=CH2 (major). Major product is Hofmann product (less substituted alkene).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Curtius rearrangement converts acyl azides to:
options: Primary amines with loss of one carbon
Isocyanates which on hydrolysis give primary amines
questions.explanation: Curtius rearrangement: R-CON3 (acyl azide) → R-N=C=O (isocyanate) + N2↑. This occurs on heating the acyl azide. The isocyanate is then hydrolyzed: R-NCO + H2O → R-NH2 + CO2. Overall: R-COOH → R-NH2 (loss of one carbon, similar to Hofmann). Key intermediate is isocyanate (same as Hofmann rearrangement). Comparison: Hofmann uses amide + Br2/OH-; Curtius uses acyl azide + heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The Schotten-Baumann reaction involves benzoylation of:
questions.explanation: Schotten-Baumann reaction: Acylation using benzoyl chloride in presence of aqueous NaOH. Conditions: Benzoyl chloride + substrate + dilute NaOH at room temperature. Used for benzoylation of: Amines (R-NH2 → R-NHCOC6H5) and Alcohols/Phenols (R-OH → R-OCOC6H5). NaOH neutralizes HCl formed and maintains basic medium. This is a test for amines and alcohols (identification reaction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The mustard oil reaction is given by:
questions.explanation: Mustard oil reaction: R-NH2 + CS2 + HgCl2 → R-N=C=S (alkyl isothiocyanate) + HgS + 2HCl. Primary amine reacts with carbon disulfide (CS2) and HgCl2. Product is alkyl isothiocyanate which has smell like mustard oil. This is a test for PRIMARY amines. Secondary amines do not give this test (no replaceable H on N after first substitution). Aromatic amines (aniline) also give this test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: PASSAGE: Amines can be prepared by various methods. The Gabriel synthesis gives pure primary amines from alkyl halides. The Hofmann degradation converts amides to amines with loss of one carbon. Reduction of nitriles gives primary amines with same carbon number. Diazonium salts are versatile intermediates for introducing substituents on aromatic rings. Based on the passage, which method would you use to prepare n-butylamine from a carboxylic acid with same carbon number?
questions.explanation: According to passage, Gabriel synthesis gives primary amines from alkyl halides with same carbon number. 1-bromobutane (4C) → n-butylamine (4C) via Gabriel synthesis. Reduction of nitriles also gives primary amines with same carbon number: Butanenitrile (4C) → n-butylamine (4C). Hofmann degradation would give propylamine (3C), not n-butylamine. Both Gabriel synthesis and nitrile reduction maintain the same carbon number.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: [Based on same passage] The Hofmann degradation of propanamide would give:
questions.explanation: According to passage, Hofmann degradation converts amides to amines with loss of one carbon. Propanamide (CH3CH2CONH2) has 3 carbons. After Hofmann degradation: CH3CH2NH2 (ethylamine) with 2 carbons. One carbon is lost as carbonate ion (CO3^2-). This is characteristic of Hofmann rearrangement - chain length decreases by one.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the strongest base?
questions.explanation: Basicity depends on availability of lone pair on nitrogen for protonation. Analysis: Aniline - Lone pair delocalized into benzene ring (resonance), less available; Cyclohexylamine - Aliphatic amine, lone pair localized on N, most available; p-Nitroaniline - NO2 is electron-withdrawing, further decreases electron density on N; Acetamide - Lone pair delocalized with carbonyl (resonance), very weak base. Cyclohexylamine has no resonance delocalization, so lone pair is most available. Order: Cyclohexylamine > Aniline > p-Nitroaniline > Acetamide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The best method to prepare pure aniline from nitrobenzene is:
questions.explanation: Nitrobenzene can be reduced to aniline by various methods: Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl (chemical reduction) followed by basification with NaOH; H2/Ni or H2/Pt (catalytic hydrogenation); LiAlH4 (strong reducing agent). All these methods convert -NO2 to -NH2. Sn/HCl or Fe/HCl gives aniline chloride, which is converted to free aniline by NaOH. Catalytic hydrogenation gives pure aniline directly. All methods are valid and give pure aniline.
